arguments.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one original earned-picture illustration for the Ukraine Atlas theme of RevealLine, gradually uncovered during a level and enjoyed as complete scenery after victory.
Format: exactly one full-bleed landscape 2:1 image, ideally 2048 by 1024 pixels. Not a contact sheet, panorama strip with panels, game screenshot or map.
Style/medium: beautiful modern pixel-art environmental illustration with deliberate square color clusters, crisp stepped contours, restrained dithering and detailed materials. Nostalgic 16-bit adventure-game sensibility, entirely original. Rich but disciplined lighting with broad shapes that remain readable at small size; selective small details reward partial reveals. No photorealism, smooth 3D rendering, painterly brush blur, vector gradients, noise filter or CRT overlay.
Shared palette: deep ink navy, muted petrol and blue-violet shadows, warm amber/apricot light, natural moss greens, creamy linen whites, selective terracotta/crimson and cornflower accents. Express illumination in clean pixel clusters; do not saturate every surface or fill the whole scene with confetti texture.
Constraints: no words, letters, digits, labels, logos, watermark or signature. No HUD, menus, targeting marks, borders, baked capture trails or UI. No copied game art, museum artwork, film frames or recognizable copyrighted characters. No bodies, gore or violence. No modern screens, powerlines, cars, tactical equipment or drones. No people necessary. Opaque complete scene fills the canvas.
Cultural approach: original illustrative scene informed by Ukrainian cultural traditions; not a photograph, museum-object replica, exact historical reconstruction or assertion that every decorative pattern is an authenticated regional motif.
Primary request: a Hutsul-inspired Carpathian homestead at misty dawn, viewed from a sheltered timber porch toward layered forest ridges and a small hillside farmyard. A richly tactile woven wool blanket draped over a carved wooden bench is the foreground focal detail: broad cream, charcoal, muted brick-red and moss geometric bands, readable stepped diamonds and fringed wool edges. Nearby doorway posts and a small wooden storage chest carry original restrained geometric carving, with tiny contrasting wood inlays on the chest, rather than copied historic motifs. Show the main log house with a steep shingled roof and protective eaves, a fence following the slope, a narrow path and a modest hay shelter, all arranged asymmetrically within a living homestead. Cool mist bands separate the receding fir-covered mountains; a small amber glow from a window and first apricot sunlight on carved wood make the shelter inviting. Strong contrast between warm near craftwork and quiet distant mountain space. Keep textile and wood texture deliberately clustered rather than granular. This particular porch, blanket pattern and mountain location are invented; the Hutsul craft references are broad, not a reconstruction of a named village.

Primary request: a radiant sunny midday Ukrainian courtyard inspired by the floral decorative tradition of Petrykivka. A whitewashed cottage wall curves gently around a peaceful garden court, with an open blue wooden gate leading toward a small orchard. The main focal surface is a broad section of white wall carrying a completely original Petrykivka-inspired composition of fantastic crimson/coral flowers, slender leaves, berry clusters and two small stylized ornamental birds; keep it a coherent airy arrangement with cream space between branches, not all-over wallpaper. Echo a smaller invented floral motif on a single wooden bowl on the near bench. Real hollyhocks and marigolds, a clay water jug and soft leaf shadows connect painted nature with the actual garden. No detached icons or museum-display labels. Architectural perspective and a sunlit stepping-stone path lead the eye across the scene; broad shade beneath the eaves balances the luminous wall. Local flora/fauna and fantastic flowers are cultural references; the particular house, mural composition, bird forms and planting are invented for this picture, not copied from any artist or known mural. Midday light should feel generous and warm without washing out the pixel-art detail.

Primary request: an illustrative Cossack-era riverside settlement and timber fort beside the Dnipro in autumn at sunset. View from a low wooded bluff looking obliquely along the bank: an earthen rampart with pointed timber palisade and simple timber watchtower encloses a modest settlement of low huts, workshops and a small central wooden church beside an open gathering space. The fortified settlement is a cultural setting, not a battle scene. A footpath descends toward a quiet landing with a couple of plain wooden rowing boats, coiled rope, reeds and drying fishing nets. Near golden oak branches and a worn wooden gatepost frame the distant water without obscuring the central landscape. Copper leaves, apricot sunlight on roof shingles, violet shadow beneath the palisade and a broad restrained reflection in the river create luminous depth. Keep the settlement human-scaled, without a massive European stone castle, fantasy towers, huge onion domes or modern buildings. No flags, insignia or weapons as focal props. This layout is a new fictional composition inspired by general Cossack settlement features; do not replicate the modern Khortytsia museum complex or any named historical fort, and do not imply a precise century, archaeological footprint or preserved event.
